direct_claims: This chart shows net electricity imports as a share of electricity demand for selected countries in 2025.
Positive values indicate countries that import more electricity than they export, while negative values indicate net exporters.
The countries shown are the United Kingdom, Germany, United States, India, Canada, France, and Sweden.
Among the countries displayed, the United Kingdom has the highest net import share at 9.05%.
Among the countries displayed, Sweden has the largest net export position at -24.51%, followed by France at -19.58%.
The chart was published by Our World in Data and cites Ember (2026) as the data source.
In electricity systems, net imports measure how much of a country's electricity demand is met by cross-border purchases after subtracting exports.
Negative values for Sweden, France, and Canada mean these countries are net suppliers to neighboring markets in the period represented.
The chart is a single-year comparison rather than a time trend, so it cannot by itself show whether a country's import dependence is rising or falling over time.
Because the values are expressed as shares of electricity demand, the chart compares trade dependence relative to system size rather than absolute electricity volumes.
